# 160 · A refill helper rewritten as whole periods, proved once and one function in its caller's proof

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **✓ Verified: equivalent on every input** | functional, no-false-positive | none | refactor, behaviour change not intended | [`RetryAfter#nanosUntilToken`](../../examples/apps/crosscut/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/crosscut/ratelimit/RetryAfter.java) | [B9: Regression verification](../../lib/README.md) |

> Crosscut's `TokenBucket.lastAfter`, the time up to which a refill has credited the bucket, is rewritten from `now - (now - last) % period` to `last + (now - last) / period * period`, the whole periods counted and added back. Its caller, the `Retry-After` of a refused request, is unchanged. Run with the proof cache, the regression proof of the caller first proves the helper's two versions equal on every input, as a check of its own, and stores that proof. It then takes the helper as one function in both versions of the caller, whose statement names the helper's proof by its claim key. Where example 120 shares a helper because its bytecode is identical, this one shares a helper that changed, on the strength of its own proof.

Tags: [resilience](../README.md#tag-resilience), [clocks-and-time](../README.md#tag-clocks-and-time), [shared-callees](../README.md#tag-shared-callees), [proved-helpers](../README.md#tag-proved-helpers), [own-checker](../README.md#tag-own-checker)

## The change

Count the whole periods since the last refill, `long periods = (nowNanos - lastNanos) / periodNanos`, and credit them, `lastNanos + periods * periodNanos`, in place of `nowNanos - (nowNanos - lastNanos) % periodNanos`, the clock less the part of a period not earned yet. The javadoc says the same in the new order. `RetryAfter`, the method checked, is unchanged, and so are the tests.

The patch leaves `RetryAfter.java` alone and changes a helper it calls, in [`TokenBucket.java`](../../examples/apps/crosscut/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/crosscut/ratelimit/TokenBucket.java).

**Before** ([`TokenBucket.java`](../../examples/apps/crosscut/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/crosscut/ratelimit/TokenBucket.java), line 18):

```java

    /**
     * The time up to which refills have been credited after the refill: {@code lastNanos} advanced by the whole
     * periods that earned a token, which is {@code nowNanos} less the part of a period that has not earned one yet.
     * That part is kept, so that a bucket polled more often than it refills still refills.
     */
    public static long lastAfter(long tokens, long lastNanos, long nowNanos, long periodNanos, long capacity) {
        return nowNanos - (nowNanos - lastNanos) % periodNanos;
    }
}
```

**After:**

```java

    /**
     * The time up to which refills have been credited after the refill: {@code lastNanos} advanced by the whole
     * periods that earned a token. The part of a period that has not earned one yet is left after it, so that a
     * bucket polled more often than it refills still refills.
     */
    public static long lastAfter(long tokens, long lastNanos, long nowNanos, long periodNanos, long capacity) {
        long periods = (nowNanos - lastNanos) / periodNanos;
        return lastNanos + periods * periodNanos;
    }
}
```

## What the verifier found

For every input, the new code returns what the old code returned, or throws what it threw.

This is a proof over the whole domain (tokens: long × lastNanos: long × nowNanos: long × periodNanos: long × capacity: long), not a sample. The tool's own checker ran the harness symbolically, path by path, with its bundled SAT solver deciding at each branch which sides are feasible, and no feasible path reaches the assertion: no input exists on which they differ.

The changed helpers, each checked before the caller (`--cache`):

- `TokenBucket.lastAfter` changed, and was proved first, as a check of its own: its two versions have the same outcome, result or exception, on every input, proved now and stored in the proof cache (claim sha256:4a6fc5dfefcdf9f776bfdb4c07f27c8cb0be09ef0eb78ad35f1f31ab1eadab3e). The caller's proof took it as one function in both versions, and its statement names that proof among its assumptions.

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

Every existing unit test passes, as it should (`java -ea net.terminalvalue.crosscut.Tests`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

None: the helper's two versions give the same credited time, or both throw `ArithmeticException` for a zero period, on every input, and the caller's proof is over every input too. What is at stake is the review of an arithmetic identity, `(d / p) * p + d % p == d`, on 64-bit values, which a reader has to trust for negative differences and for the one overflowing quotient, `Long.MIN_VALUE / -1`.

## Why the verdict is right

The proof runs with a proof cache, a fresh directory under the build (`--cache`). Before the caller's proof, the tool looks at the static callees both versions call. `TokenBucket.tokensAfter` is identical in both, so it is one function in both as in example 120. `TokenBucket.lastAfter` changed. It is in the narrow class a proof of its own may stand for: static, a pure function of `long`s, no exception of its own (only a zero period's `ArithmeticException`), no static initializer, and not trivial (a remainder, a division and a product). So the tool checks it first as a check of its own: the same builds and settings, `lastAfter` as the target, nothing restricting its inputs. The own checker proves that check: the product of a quotient and its divisor is the dividend less the remainder, exactly (example 138), so both versions compute the same bits. The proof is stored in the cache under its claim key. The caller's proof then redirects the previous version's calls of `lastAfter` to the new version's method, and proves `nanosUntilToken` with one `lastAfter` in both versions. Its statement has an assumption of kind `callee`, basis `proved`, whose id is the helper proof's claim key. Since the caller's claim key digests that assumption, a different helper proof gives the caller a different key.

## What to do

Merge. The proof of the helper says the two forms credit the same time, and the caller's proof says the `Retry-After` is unchanged with it.

## Notes

- Why the proof can take the helper's new version for both: the helper's own proof is over every input of its parameter types, so every call, in either version and with any arguments, is in its domain, and the two versions have the same outcome there, a result or the same exception. Neither reads or writes state. The previous version with its calls redirected therefore behaves exactly as written, and the caller's proof is exact: a counterexample under the redirection would be a real one, and no refinement is needed. A helper proof over a narrower domain (`--unchanged-unless`, mapped arguments, a relation between results) is never used, since it would need an assertion at each call.
- Measured when the example was written, on the development machine: the helper's proof took 0.19 s (2 paths, 2 solver calls), and the caller's with the helper as one function 0.00 s (3 paths, 2 solver calls). Without the cache, the caller's proof runs through both versions of the helper as written and takes 1.2 s (4 solver calls) for the same verdict. A second run with the same cache is an exact hit of the caller's claim, and a second caller of the helper would find the helper's proof in the cache. The recorded run starts from an empty cache, so its proof line says the helper was proved now.
- The helper's proof is a regression proof like any other, and its key is the one a check of `TokenBucket#lastAfter` alone gets: the library's tests check both, and that a caller's key does not depend on when or where the helper's proof was made.
- Without `--cache` the tool proves nothing of a changed helper, and runs the caller through both versions of it, which is what every recorded example did before this one. The cache is the proof's only source of helper evidence, and it is local: a directory under the build, filled by this run and never committed.
- Example 161 is the sibling with the helper's change wrong: its own proof is refuted, the helper stays as written, and the caller's proof finds the regression.
- Gap scan (step 1a of `llm-dlc/loops/sound-verdicts.md`, 7 November 2026, JDK 25.0.5, from the bytecode, nothing proved): the tool's own checker meets no gap in the 3 methods the proof reaches in either version, so strict mode does not move this verdict.
- Until 2026-11-07 the pipeline job for this example stopped before any proof, because the patch leaves the subject file `RetryAfter.java` alone (VF-016). Since the cleanup loop's examples stream, `build.py`'s `excerpts()` takes such a subject when the patch changes one Java file of its source tree that the subject's source names by its class, here `TokenBucket.java`: the page shows that file's hunks and says so, and the subject, the verified unit and the SARIF location stay `RetryAfter`. The job is resubmitted as `20261107-163050-example-160-a-changed-refill-helper-prov`.
- Seen 2026-11-07 (VF-016, second run): job `20261107-163050-example-160-a-changed-refill-helper-prov`, at `d32ddc64`, got past the subject check, ran the proof and failed validating the result: `build.py` writes `proofCache` in the claim's scope for a proof with the proof cache, and `result.schema.json` didn't allow it. The schema now does (`test_build.py`'s `test_a_claim_that_may_rest_on_helpers_proofs_validates_against_the_schema`). The job's recorded `jvmcontract` output, replayed through `run_tool_equivalence`, gives verified, with `TokenBucket.lastAfter` shared, and its fields validate. The job is resubmitted once more, as `20261107-165152-example-160-a-changed-refill-helper-prov`.

## Evidence

How the verdict was reached: jvmcontract's own checker (CaDiCaL): 1 properties proved over tokens: long × lastNanos: long × nowNanos: long × periodNanos: long × capacity: long in 0.0 s; loops unwound 16 times with unwinding assertions; TokenBucket.lastAfter changed, its two versions proved to have the same outcome on every input (claim sha256:4a6fc5dfefcdf9f776bfdb4c07f27c8cb0be09ef0eb78ad35f1f31ab1eadab3e), and taken as one function in both.

**What the verdict is about.** For every input in `tokens: long × lastNanos: long × nowNanos: long × periodNanos: long × capacity: long`, assuming TokenBucket.lastAfter(long, long, long, long, long), changed, is one function in both versions: a regression proof of its own (claim sha256:4a6fc5dfefcdf9f776bfdb4c07f27c8cb0be09ef0eb78ad35f1f31ab1eadab3e) shows its two versions give the same result or throw the same exception on every input of its parameter types, so every call in either version is in that proof's domain (a changed helper's own regression proof, made by the tool's own checker before the caller's and kept in its proof cache); every JDK class is initialized already, its static initializer having run and thrown nothing (the checker's own semantics): the two versions agree on the result, equal in both versions, and on exceptions: whether it throws, and which of 15 exception classes it throws (NumberFormatException, ArithmeticException, NullPointerException and the rest; another class counts as the first of them it is an instance of), the same in both versions; the message and the exception's state are not compared. Loops are unwound up to 16 times, every one shown to end within that; the search covered every execution of every input within these bounds. Checked by jvmcontract's own checker (CaDiCaL), SAT solver CaDiCaL 1.9.5 (bundled), under --gaps strict. It read the tool's 17 models of JDK classes (`sha256:94d88f1eba1010b636526723c1ac63793fefa0f6d6cd628953b3e423fa2b89a1`) and the classes of JDK 25.0.5. Nothing skips an input in the domain before the calls, so the verdict is about every one of them.

- [The Java Language Specification, 15.17.2 and 15.17.3: division truncates toward zero and the remainder satisfies (a / b) * b + (a % b) == a](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se21/html/jls-15.html#jls-15.17.2)
